la:verb:progredior.gloss: to come, go, or march forth, forward or on; advance, proceed
senses: to come, go, or march forth, forward or on; advance, proceed
to make progress, advance, develop, proceed, go on; advance in age, get older
la:verb:progredior.html:
prō-grĕdĭor, gressus, 3 (collat. form, acc. to the fourth conj.,
inf. progrediri, ; imp. progredimino, ; act. collat. form, v.infrafin.), v. dep. a. [gradior], to come or go forth, to go or march forward, go on, advance, proceed (class.; syn.: prodeo, proficiscor).
Lit.: ut regredi quam progredi mallent,: si quo hic gradietur, pariter progrediminor,: foras,; : pedetemptim,: ex domo,: longius a castris,: in locum iniquum,: tridui viam progressi,; ; : ad Inalpinos cum exercitu, Brut. ap. : ante signa,: obviam alicui,—
Trop.: nunc ad reliqua progrediar,will proceed,: procedere et progredi in virtute,: cum autem progrediens confirmatur animus, agnoscit ille quidem naturae vim, sed ita ut progredi possit longius, id.

; so, longius progredi,to go on,: quoad progredi potuerit feri hominis amentia,: videamus, quatenus amor in amicitiā progredi debeat,: divinatio conjecturā nititur, ultra quam progredi non potest,: progredientibus aetatibus,: paulum aetate progressus,advanced in age, become older,: in adulationem progressus,: quo amentiae progressi sunt,: paulum aliquid ultra primas litteras progressi,; cf.: incipientibus aut paulum progressis,.—Hence, prōgressus, a, um, P. a., advanced: progressā aetate,.—Comp.: ut progressior reverteretur anima,: progressioris aetatis sum,.—Act. collat. form, prōgrĕdĭo, īre, to go forward, etc. (ante-class.): age, move te, in navem primus progredi, Nov. ap. .

la:noun:prognosticon.gloss: a prognostication; an omen or sign of the future
senses: a prognostication; an omen or sign of the future
la:noun:prognosticon.html:
prŏgnōstĭcon or -um, i, n., = προγνωστικόν,
a sign or token of the future, a prognostic; hence, prŏgnōstĭca, ōrum, n., the signs of the weather, .— Also as the title of Cicero's translation of the Προγνωστικά of Aratus, ; v. the fragments, id. Op. v. XI. p. 96 sqq. B. and K.

la:noun:progressus.html:
prōgressus, ūs, m.
progredior
,
a going forward, advance, progress (class.).
Lit.: (Antonium) Brutus progressu arcuit,.—Of the planets: progressus et regressus constantes,: progressum praecipitem, inconstantem reditum videt,. —*
Transf., concr., a jetty, pier, mole, .—
Trop.
Advancement, progress, growth, increase, etc.: aetatis,: primo progressu, at the first outset, i. e. at the very commencement, : in studiis progressus facere,; cf.: progressus habere in Stoicis,: tantum progressum facere,.—
In partic., course, progress, of events: homo causas rerum videt, earumque progressus et quasi antecessiones non ignorat,.

la:verb:progredio.gloss: to come, go, or march forth, forward or on; advance, proceed

la:noun:progenies.html:
prōgĕnĭes, ēi (archaic
gen. sing. progenii, Pac. ap. ; and id. ap. ), f.
progigno
, descent, lineage, race, family.
Lit.: in abstracto (very rare but class.): progeniem vestram usque ab avo atque atavo proferens,: antiquitas quo propius aberat ab ortu et divinā progenie, hoc melius, etc.,; : virtutem, non progeniem quaeri oportere (preceded by qui modo esset Herculis stirpe generatus),: progeniem sed enim Trojano a sanguine duci,.—
Transf., in concr.
Descendants, posterity, offspring, progeny, a son or daughter, a child (the predom. signification of the word; syn.: proles, suboles), Epitaphs of the Scipios: veteres, qui se progeniem deorum esse dicebant,: Priamum tantā progenie (i.e. quinquaginta filiis) orbatum,: progenies mea, Claudia,; so, Sarpedon, mea progenies,: Bacchum Progeniem negat esse Jovis, Ov M. 4, 3; : progenies quoque, ut Apollo ac Diana Latonae,: ex magnā progenie liberorum (preceded by ex tantā stirpe liberūm),; cf. : cum se matura levabit progenies (avium),.—In plur.: duces ducumque progenies, (30), 4.—
A generation of men (eccl. Lat.): una,; .—
Of animals, offspring, young, etc., ; ; ; .—Transf., of plants: vitis progenies,.—
Trop., of poems, as offsprings of the poet's mind (poet.): stirps haec progeniesque mea est,.

la:verb:progigno.html:
prō-gigno, gĕnŭi, gĕnĭtum, 3, v. a.,
to beget, bear, bring forth, produce (rare but class.): neque natus est neque progignetur,: in seminibus vis inest earum rerum, quae ex iis progignuntur,: illam terra parens Progenuit,: te saevae progenuere ferae,: sensum progignere acerbum, : novos motus rerum,: quia nolebam ex me morem progigni malum,; v. Ritschl ad h. l.: Eurotae progignunt flumina myrtus,.

la:noun:progenitor.html:
prōgĕnĭtor, ōris, m.
id.
,
the founder of a family, an ancestor, progenitor (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): si tui veretur te progenitoris, Att. ap. : Eurysthenes progenitor majorum suorum,: deūm, Val. Soran. ap. , 7, 11; ; plur., ; .

la:noun:progressio.html:
prōgressĭo, ōnis, f.
progredior
,
a going forth or forward, progression; trop., advancement, progress, growth, increase (a favorite word with Cicero).
In gen.: omnium rerum principia parva sunt, sed suis progressionibus usa augentur,; cf. : progressionem, virtutem persequi,: progressio admirabilis ad omnem excellentiam,: progressionem facere ad virtutem,: discendi,.—
In partic., a figure of speech, a progression, climax, i. e. a progressive strengthening of expressions, ; .

la:adj:prognatus.html:
prō-gnātus, a, um, Part. [gnatus, natus, from nascor],
born, descended, sprung from some one; of children or descendants.
Lit.: CORNELIVS LVCIVS SCIPIO BARBATVS GNAIVOD PATRE PROGNATVS, first Epitaph of the Scipios; SO, PROGNATVM PVBLIO, ninth Epitaph of the Scipios: corpore Tartarino (i. e. Chao) prognata Paluda virago (i. e. Minerva, Aër), Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 510 Vahl.): Sosiam Davo prognatum patre,: a meo patre prognatus,: bonis prognatam,; ; : Romulus deo prognatus,.—As subst.: prōgnātus, i, m., a child, descendant (ante-class.): parentes, Patria et prognati,children,: Herculei prognati,the descendants of Hercules,; cf.: Tantalo prognatus, Pelope natus,i. e. Atreus, grandson of Tantalus,: ex Cimbris Teutonisque prognati,: Galli ab Dite patre prognati,: Venere, Cael. ap. : Delphis prognatus Pythius Apollo,: quali genere prognatus?: Castor gaudet equis, ovo prognatus eodem Pugnis,.—
Transf., of plants, sprung or grown forth: Peliaco quondam prognatae vertice pinus,: harundines in palude prognatae,.
